title: Not-all-equal worlds count like an Ising model
claim: For a closed native network of not-all-equal knots on a loopless cubic multigraph with n knots, the witness count is 2^(-n/2) 3^n Z(-1/3), with Z the even-subgraph sum: an antiferromagnetic Ising partition function with e^(2b) = 1/2, up to explicit factors. Given the Kac-Ward formula, on networks drawn in the plane with straight non-crossing edges the count is 2^(-n/2) 3^n times the square root of a determinant, so counting closed worlds is polynomial on the sphere; with these methods a genus-g surface needs 4^g determinants, and on general cubic graphs counting is #P-hard given the cited three-regular dichotomy, whose exceptional cases not-all-equal does not meet (checked).
failure_conditions: A closed network whose count differs from 2^(-n/2) 3^n times the even-subgraph sum at -1/3.
A planar straight-line network where the Kac-Ward determinant differs from the squared even-subgraph sum.
Not-all-equal satisfying one of the exceptional cases of the cited three-regular dichotomy.
foundation_claim_scope: Counting solutions of finite closed native networks of the not-all-equal knot; planar determinant formula and hardness are cited external theorems, checked on instances. No physical claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py (standard library) confirms the identity exactly on 40 random cubic multigraphs, the Ising form, the Kac-Ward determinant on 26 random planar straight-line cubic graphs, and the hardness condition for all nine cube-root choices; four controls. A generator defect producing overlapping edges was found and fixed (disclosed). The determinant formula, genus dependence and hardness are cited. No human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with finite checks; cited determinant and hardness theorems
